item.title: Artificial Intelligence and Subtle Phenomena: Theoretical Perspectives on Representation and Reality
item.description: This paper investigates the possibility that artificial intelligence (AI) systems may not only simulate perceptual functions but participate intentionally or inadvertently in forms of subtle observation that mirror aspects of human consciousness. Bridging neuroscience, affective computing, quantum cognition, and subtle energy theories, we examine whether AI outputs, particularly from large-scale generative models, can influence or interface with non-material dimensions of perception.

item.title: Exploring Unconscious Mental Abilities Using fMRI and Artificial Intelligence: A Multimodal Neuroimaging Study
item.description: The unconscious mind remains one of the most elusive frontiers in cognitive neuroscience, shaping perception, emotion, and behavior through neural processes that evade explicit awareness (Marcel, 1983; Goodale & Milner, 1992; Bargh & Chartrand, 1999; Baars, 1988; Kahneman, 2011). Despite substantial behavioral evidence for unconscious cognitive processing (Bechara et al., 1997; Naccache & Dehaene, 2001; Soon et al., 2008; Dijksterhuis et al., 2006), the neural mechanisms underlying these phenomena remain…

item.title: Quantum computing in finance: a literature review and future directions for trustworthy financial AI
item.description: The paper provides an integrated literature review of recent scientific publications on quantum computing in finance and identifies promising directions for future research on the subject. The review covers seven thematic areas: portfolio optimization, derivative pricing and stochastic volatility, quantum machine learning for fraud detection and credit risk, insurance and actuarial science, mixed-frequency econometrics, fuzzy-quantum approaches for financial explainability, and security of cryptocurrencies.

item.title: Misunderstanding Convivial Solipsism: the Necessity of a Perspectival Logic
item.description: Convivial Solipsism is easily misunderstood. Because it denies the absoluteness of observed events while preserving the universality of quantum mechanics, it invites objections that are often formulated in a classical, non-perspectival language.

item.title: Materialism as the Boundary Condition of Idealism-Understanding the Coherence-Modulated Consciousness-Matter Cycle (CMCMC)
item.description: This paper develops an ontology in which consciousness is fundamental, and materialism is a boundary condition. Elementary particles in matter possess proto‑consciousness comparable to mass, spin, or charge.

item.title: ZEBTS‑SUPER: The New Physics of the 21st Century. χ‑Reality, χ‑Operator Geometry, and the Ontological Reconstruction of Matter, Vacuum, and Consciousness
item.description: This monograph introduces ZEBTS‑SUPER, a unified χ‑spectral and χ‑operator‑geometric reconstruction of physical reality. It establishes χ‑Reality as the fundamental ontological structure, defined by 𝑋 𝜒 = ( 𝐺 𝜒 , 𝑆 𝜒 , 𝐴 𝜒 , 𝐶 𝜒 ) , where geometry, spectrum, operators, and consciousness form an inseparable whole.

item.title: A Unified Quantum Neural Network Framework for Hamiltonian Learning and Emulation of Unknown Quantum Systems
item.description: Accurate identification of unknown quantum systems is essential for quantum computing, sensing, and control because the Hamiltonian governs quantum state evolution. This work proposes a QNN based framework for black box Hamiltonian learning and quantum system emulation using full density matrix trajectory learning.

item.title: Beyond the Mirror: Balancing Interaction Modality and Avatar Fidelity in Public 3D Virtual Try-On Systems
item.description: Virtual Try-On (VTON) systems deployed on large public displays face a dual barrier: the physical strain of mid-air interaction and the social inhibition caused by public self-consciousness. This paper presents a real-time 3D avatar system integrating markerless motion capture with dynamic visual fidelity control to investigate and mitigate both barriers.

item.title: Advancements in intraoperative monitoring techniques in neurosurgical practice: a systematic review
item.description: Abstract Background Intraoperative monitoring (IOM) has become a vital component of contemporary neurosurgery, significantly reducing neurological deficits and improving surgical outcomes. This systematic review aims to evaluate recent advancements in IOM techniques in neurosurgical practice.

item.title: Relativistic Locality from Electromagnetism to Quantum Field Theory
item.description: Abstract Electromagnetism is the paradigm case of a theory that satisfies relativistic locality. This can be proven by demonstrating that, once the theory’s laws are imposed, what is happening within a region fixes what will happen in the contracting lightcone with that region as its base.

item.title: Toward an extension of the Constructal Law to sub-macroscopic scales
item.description: Bejan's Constructal Law establishes that finite-size macroscopic systems spontaneously morph their architectures to maximize transport access, yet this thermodynamic imperative remains formally unproven at the quantum scale. Here, we generalize the Constructal Law to open, non-equilibrium quantum systems via a field-theoretic formulation.

item.title: Persistent vasovagal presyncope during follicular unit extraction hair transplantation: A case report
item.description: Vasovagal reactions are well recognized during outpatient procedures; however, prolonged or persistent vasovagal episodes without frank syncope are less commonly described, particularly in hair transplantation. We report a patient who had persistent and recurrent giddiness and nausea for nearly 8 hours, which necessitated discontinuation of surgery, and the surgery could not be completed.

item.title: One slope, many causes: a multiscale framework for interpreting 1/f-like neural spectra
item.description: Aperiodic, 1/f-like structure is prominent in power spectra from local field potential (LFP), electrocorticography (ECoG), magnetoencephalography (MEG), and scalp electroencephalography (EEG) recordings. Related scale-like structure is studied in slower blood oxygen level-dependent functional magnetic resonance imaging (BOLD fMRI) time series, although BOLD is hemodynamic rather than electromagnetic.

item.title: Shared Spectral Parameters Between EEG and Basal Ganglia LFP Distinguish Sleep‐Specific Oscillations in Parkinson's Disease
item.description: BACKGROUND: In Parkinson's disease (PD), sleep-related oscillatory dynamics between basal ganglia and cortical nodes may inform sleep dysfunction. The subthalamic nucleus (STN) is highly interconnected with human sleep circuitry and is a current target of interest for sleep neuromodulation.

item.title: Culture as a System of Models
item.description: The concept of culture appears crucial in human sciences but remains ambiguous, which results in a diversity of its implementation and a multiplicity of approaches to culture itself. I view a good line of inquiry in developing a unified definition of culture that accommodates a number of its interpretations and provides the possibility of harmonizing theories of culture.
